pageProps.title: Open Darkness
pageProps.review: A book review exploring the elaborate tricks and motives unique to Japanese mystery novels through Renjo Mikihiko's short mystery stories, featuring the author's original charm and curiosity-inducing twists.
pageProps.description: An invitation to unpretentious desires that cross between passionate longing and cold revenge—break what you cannot have, deceive what you cannot trust, and kill what you cannot save.
pageProps.content:
## Review I started reading this book after being impressed by Renjo Mikihiko's ```7-in-1 Role``` and wanting to explore more of his work. I didn't realize it was a short story collection, so I spent a lot of effort taking notes on all the characters as I read. I was a bit disappointed when I realized they were short stories...
They were typical Japanese mystery novels focused on finding motives and tricks. However, the collection was full of short stories that evoked the same intense curiosity about the tricks as ```7-in-1 Role``` did.
